catalog_quote: Phonologically, Tiddim Chin has three contrastive tones with relatively complex tone sandhi, as well as several intonation patterns. ... As shown in Table 3, Tiddim Chin has three distinctive tones: a rising tone, a level tone, and a falling tone. The pitch of each tone varies according to vowel length and the sonority of a syllable-final consonant. ... 2.2 Syllable structure Tiddim Chin's syllable structure can be reduced to (C1) (V1) V2 (V3) (C2) / T, where C1 represents an onset consonant, V represents a vowel, C2 represents a coda consonant, and T represents a tone. Each syllable consists of a vowel and may include an onset and a coda. A majority of Tiddim Chin morphemes are phonologically monosyllabic (e.g., nê¹ "eat"), though a few show a disyllabic combination of two monosyllabic structures (e.g., pa³tâu³ "nervous"). ... sources.citation: Ostapirat, Weera. 1998. Tiddim Chin tones in historical perspective. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 21(1): 235-248. doi:10.32655/ltba.21.1.06
sources.quote: 'Tiddim Chin shows three tones in smooth syllables (syllables ending with sonorants and vowels): rising, level and falling, which are numbered by Henderson (1965) as tones 1, 2 and 3 respectively. Long checked syllables ... also occur with these three tones. Short checked syllables only occur with a low level tone, which has been considered to be an allotone of tone 3.' No mention of word stress/accent anywhere (grep of scanned: 'stress'/'accent'/'promin' occur only in non-prosodic senses).
